name: Abyssal
description: A deep-ocean survey programme mapping the seafloor below 3,000 metres. Open data, open instruments, open ship time.
canvasAlt: A dark teal gradient sweeping slowly across the page, like water moving under a light

sections.heading: Below three thousand metres
sections.body: Abyssal is a shared survey programme. We put instruments on the seabed, leave them there, and publish everything they record.

sections.heading: Landers built to be lost
sections.body: Each lander is cheap enough that losing one is a bad week rather than a bad year. Aluminium frame, glass spheres, an acoustic release and a strobe.

sections.heading: Down in ninety minutes, up when called
sections.body: A lander free-falls to the seabed under ballast and sits recording until a ship returns and calls it back. Most come back. Some do not.

sections.heading: Most of the seafloor has never been measured, only estimated
Raw first, tidy later
sections.body: Every recording is published as it came off the instrument, before anyone cleans it. The processing scripts go up beside it so the steps are auditable.

sections.heading: Berths for people outside the programme
sections.body: Every cruise carries places for researchers with no funding of their own. Bring an instrument that fits the frame and we will drop it for you.

sections.heading: Tell us what you would measure
sections.body: Send the instrument, the depth it needs and how long it has to sit there. The next deployment window and what is already on the frame are both public.
